question: Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=5x-7$. Show that $f$ is one-one.
explanation:
Equality of images
Let $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}$ and suppose $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$. Then
$$5x_1-7=5x_2-7.$$

Simplification
Adding $7$ to both sides gives
$$5x_1=5x_2.$$
Dividing by $5$, we obtain
$$x_1=x_2.$$

One-one criterion
Since $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$ implies $x_1=x_2$, the function $f$ is one-one.

options.A: $f$ is not one-one because every real number has an image
options.C: $f$ is one-one only when its domain is restricted to non-negative real numbers
